summary: This Refero guide collects web implementation details that separate polished products from rough ones, which it says most AI models miss. It covers focus states (:focus-visible, never bare outline: none, :focus-within for compound controls), form attributes (type, inputmode, autocomplete, spellcheck, clickable labels, placeholder format, submit states, inline errors, unsaved-changes warning), images (explicit dimensions, fetchpriority and lazy loading), touch details, performance patterns (virtualizing 50+ item lists, avoiding layout reads in render, uncontrolled inputs, preconnect and font preload), accessibility quick wins, URL state and destructive-action confirmation, plus short copy rules. It ends with an anti-pattern list for code review and a pre-ship checklist. For a design system it is a component-implementation checklist that keeps accessibility floors and interaction quality in shipped web code.
key_ideas: Use :focus-visible so focus rings show for keyboard users, not on mouse clicks.
Never remove the outline without a visible custom focus replacement.
Use :focus-within to highlight a compound control when any child is focused.
Correct input type, inputmode and autocomplete bring up the right mobile keyboard and help password managers.
Images without width and height cause layout shift; load hero images eagerly and lower images lazily.
touch-action: manipulation removes the mobile tap delay; overscroll-behavior: contain stops scroll chaining in modals.
Autofocus only on desktop, at most one primary input per page, and only with a reason.
Virtualize lists of 50+ items and avoid reading layout during render.
Use semantic button and link elements, keyboard handlers for custom controls, and an unbroken heading order.
Reflect filters, tabs and pagination in the URL and use real links so Cmd+click and back work.
Destructive actions need a confirmation or an undo window.
Flag transition: all, disabled zoom, div buttons, unlabelled inputs and icon buttons without aria-label in code review.

claims.claim: :focus triggers on any focus including mouse clicks, while :focus-visible only triggers for keyboard navigation.
Removing outline on focus without a replacement breaks keyboard navigation.
Correct input types trigger the right keyboard on mobile, and meaningful names help password managers.
Blocking paste is an accessibility violation and user hostile.
Images are the number one cause of layout shift (CLS).
touch-action: manipulation removes the 300ms tap delay on mobile.
Reading offsetHeight in render forces synchronous layout recalculation.
Controlled inputs re-render on every keystroke; uncontrolled inputs do not.
onClick navigation breaks Cmd+click and middle-click.
user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1 disables zoom and is an accessibility violation.

quotes: Images are the #1 cause of layout shift (CLS). Fix them.
These patterns are the difference between "works" and "feels right."

rules.rule: Style focus rings with :focus-visible, not :focus, for example a 2px outline in the primary color with a 2px offset.
rules.why: :focus also fires on mouse click, which is annoying; :focus-visible fires only for keyboard navigation.

rules.rule: Never set outline: none without a visible replacement such as a two-ring box-shadow on :focus-visible.
rules.why: It breaks keyboard navigation.

rules.rule: Use :focus-within on compound controls, such as a search input with an icon, to highlight the wrapper.
rules.why: Focus on any child should highlight the parent.

rules.rule: Set the correct input type, inputmode and autocomplete on every field (email, tel, url, numeric; current-password for login, new-password for signup; off for non-auth fields). Give fields meaningful name attributes.
rules.why: Correct types trigger the right mobile keyboard, and meaningful names help password managers.

rules.rule: Never block paste in inputs.
rules.why: It is an accessibility violation and user hostile.

rules.rule: Turn spellcheck off for emails, codes, usernames and URLs.
rules.why: The source lists these fields for spellcheck off; it gives no further reason.

rules.rule: Make labels clickable and let a checkbox and its label share a single hit target with no dead zone between them.
rules.why: Clickable labels and a shared checkbox hit target leave no dead zones between control and label.

rules.rule: End placeholders with an ellipsis and show the expected format.
rules.why: Placeholders should show format.

rules.rule: Keep the submit button enabled until the request starts, then disable it and show a spinner.
rules.why: Shows submission state.

rules.rule: Show errors inline, tie them to inputs with aria-invalid and aria-describedby, use role="alert", and focus the first error on submit.
rules.why: The source shows this as the correct pattern without stating a reason.

rules.rule: Warn before the user leaves a page with unsaved changes.
rules.why: Prevents lost work [inferred].

rules.rule: Always set width and height on images.
rules.why: It reserves space and prevents layout shift.

rules.rule: Load above-the-fold images with fetchpriority="high" (priority in Next.js) and lazy-load images below the fold.
rules.why: Loading strategy by position.

rules.rule: Set touch-action: manipulation to remove the mobile tap delay.
rules.why: Removes the 300ms tap delay.

rules.rule: Set the tap highlight color intentionally instead of just disabling it.
rules.why: Set intentionally, don't just disable.

rules.rule: Set overscroll-behavior: contain on modals, drawers and sheets.
rules.why: Prevents scroll chaining.

rules.rule: Autofocus only on desktop, on at most one primary input per page, and only when justified.
rules.why: On mobile it opens the keyboard unexpectedly.

rules.rule: Virtualize lists with 50+ items, or use content-visibility: auto with contain-intrinsic-size for simpler cases.
rules.why: Prevents jank.

rules.rule: Do not read layout (offsetHeight) during render; use ResizeObserver or CSS.
rules.why: It forces synchronous layout recalculation.

rules.rule: Prefer uncontrolled inputs and read the value on submit when possible.
rules.why: Controlled inputs re-render on every keystroke.

rules.rule: Preconnect to asset and font domains and preload critical fonts.
rules.why: Performance pattern.

rules.rule: Use <button> for actions and <a> for navigation instead of clickable div or span.
rules.why: Semantic elements are a high-impact accessibility win.

rules.rule: Give custom interactive elements role, tabIndex={0} and Enter/Space key handlers.
rules.why: Interactive custom elements need keyboard support.

rules.rule: Keep heading levels in order without skipping (h1, h2, h3).
rules.why: Skipping levels is wrong.

rules.rule: Set scroll-margin-top on anchor targets to the fixed header height plus a buffer.
rules.why: Prevents the fixed header from covering anchor targets.

rules.rule: Announce async updates such as toasts and validation messages with role="status" aria-live="polite".
rules.why: Async updates need announcements.

rules.rule: Keep filters, tabs and pagination in the URL.
rules.why: Users expect to bookmark, share and use the back button.

rules.rule: Use real links, not onClick handlers, for navigation.
rules.why: onClick navigation breaks Cmd+click and middle-click.

rules.rule: Put a confirmation modal or an undo window in front of destructive actions.
rules.why: Immediate destructive actions are an anti-pattern.

rules.rule: Write copy in active voice and second person ("Your account"), use Title Case for headings and buttons, numerals for counts ("8 deployments"), specific labels ("Save API Key" not "Continue"), errors that include the fix, and & instead of "and" where space is tight.
rules.why: Content copy rules that convert.

rules.rule: Never disable zoom with user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1.
rules.why: It is an accessibility violation.

rules.rule: Do not use transition: all.
rules.why: It is a performance killer and unpredictable.

rules.rule: Give every icon-only button an aria-label and every input a label.
rules.why: Missing labels are an accessibility fail.

rules.rule: Format dates and numbers with Intl.DateTimeFormat and Intl.NumberFormat instead of hardcoding.
rules.why: Hardcoded formats are an anti-pattern.

decisions.question: When people delete something, should they confirm first or get an undo?

options.name: Confirmation modal
options.effect: An extra step before the action runs.
options.when: Destructive actions such as deleting an account.

options.name: Undo window
options.effect: The action runs, and a toast offers "Undo (10s)".
options.when: When the action can be reversed for a short time.

decisions.recommendation: Either a confirmation or an undo window; never immediate.

decisions.question: Sentence case or Title Case for headings and buttons?
decisions.recommendation: Title Case for headings and buttons.

decisions.question: Should the submit button ever be disabled?

options.name: Enabled until the request starts
options.effect: Clickable while filling in; shows a spinner and disables during submission.

decisions.recommendation: Enabled until the request starts, then disabled with a spinner.

process.detail: During code review flag disabled zoom, paste blocking, transition: all, bare outline: none, div navigation, div buttons, images without dimensions, unvirtualized 50+ lists, unlabelled inputs, icon buttons without aria-label, hardcoded formats and unjustified autoFocus.
Check focus, form attributes and labels, image dimensions and lazy loading, touch settings, list virtualization, semantic HTML and headings, URL state and links, and copy rules.

caveats: Web and React specific; native platforms are not covered.
Library recommendations (virtua, react-window, nuqs, Next.js Image) are examples, not requirements.
